canonical_statement: ParaTempo defines temporal confidence as the exponentiated negative entropy of the average intermediate answer distribution over a sliding window of recent probes.

exposures.details: C_i,t = exp(-H(g_i,t)); g_i,t averages recent probe distributions over window W

canonical_statement: ParaTempo begins with a warmup phase and sets an instance-specific pruning threshold from a quantile of temporal-confidence values observed during warmup.
After warmup, ParaTempo prunes a branch when its temporal confidence falls below the calibrated pruning threshold, releasing that computation slot for further exploration.

ParaTempo retires a branch when its dominant-answer probability remains at or above the retirement threshold for X consecutive probes; retired branches stop decoding but retain their answer and confidence weight for final aggregation.

When pruning releases a computation slot, ParaTempo can fork from the eligible donor branch with the highest temporal confidence; the fork inherits the donor prefix and continues with an independent sampling seed.
ParaTempo uses confidence-weighted voting across eligible active and retired branches and can terminate globally when the dominant answer accumulates sufficient aggregate confidence.

Figure 2 depicts ParaTempo as asynchronous branch execution with an initial warmup followed by branch-local probe, retire, prune, fork, finish, and final vote operations without width-wise synchronization.
The main experiments evaluated ParaTempo on AIME 2026, HMMT November 2025, HMMT February 2026, and GPQA Diamond using Qwen3.5-35B-A3B and GPT-OSS-20B.
